Mansa Devi (three-headed, five-armed form in the inner shrine)

history.dynasty: Maharaja Gopal Singh of Mani Majra (Sikh ruler of Mani Majra)
history.summary: Mansa Devi Temple stands atop Bilwa Parvat in the Sivalik Hills and is the famous wish-fulfilling (Mansa = wish) Shakti shrine of Haridwar, also known as Bilwa Tirth and one of the Panch Tirth (Five Pilgrimages) of Haridwar. The present temple was built by Maharaja Gopal Singh of Mani Majra in 1811-1815. The inner shrine houses two images of the goddess: one with eight arms and one with three heads and five arms. It is one of the three Siddh Peeths of Haridwar (with Chandi Devi and Maya Devi), where sincere desires are believed to be fulfilled; devotees tie threads to a sacred tree when making a wish and return to untie them once it is granted. The hilltop is reached by the 540-metre Mansa Devi Udankhatola ropeway (climbing 178 metres in about 5 minutes) or by a steep 1.5-3 km trek. Coordinates are the published Wikipedia coordinates, since the hilltop shrine has no dedicated geocoder entry.

name: Mansa Devi Temple
town_description: Haridwar, in the Haridwar district of Uttarakhand at the foothills of the Sivalik Hills where the Ganga enters the plains, is one of Hinduism's seven holy cities (Sapta Puri) and one of the four Kumbh Mela sites. Its spiritual heart is Har Ki Pauri, where the evening Ganga Aarti draws thousands daily. Mansa Devi and Chandi Devi temples crown the twin hills (Bilwa Parvat and Neel Parvat) overlooking the city, while the Maya Devi temple sits near Birla Ghat and Daksheshwar Mahadev lies in the adjoining heritage township of Kankhal.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 35-40 km; taxis and pre-paid cabs available).
travel.railway: Haridwar Junction (approx. 2-3 km; autos, e-rickshaws and taxis to the ropeway base).
travel.road: The Mansa Devi Udankhatola ropeway base station is near the city markets/Har Ki Pauri area; round-trip tickets approx. Rs. 100-145 (combo with Chandi Devi approx. Rs. 349). Alternatively trek 1.5-3 km uphill (approx. 786 steps); beware of monkeys on the path.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for comfortable weather; Navratri is the most auspicious and the most crowded period. Early mornings are quietest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opening hours conflict across sources (verify): 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM with a midday closure 12:00 PM-2:00 PM (most sources; winter hours reportedly 6 AM-8 PM) vs 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM (some sources). Ropeway typically runs 7:00 AM-12:00 PM and 2:00 PM-7:00 PM. No temple entry fee.
